concept.description: Tidewell is a fictional coastal sensor-data API: a concept page with sample data. One glass lattice that answers your cursor, then morphs through query, index, scale, ship and pricing.

copy.title: Read the whole coast
copy.deck: Tidewell stores every gauge, buoy and mooring as a point in one space you can ask about. Move your cursor over it. That is a query.

copy.title: Ask by place,
copy.deck: Every station becomes a point and a question becomes a point too. The answer is whoever sits nearest. Filter by water body to narrow the field.

copy.title: Four layers,
copy.deck: Stations are linked into layers of proximity. A search enters at the sparse top layer and walks down, visiting only a sliver of the data. One knob trades recall for latency.
copy.fine: Sample curve on sample stations. Not measured.

copy.line:
A coast has a shape.
Tidewell keeps it.
copy.caption: Illustration slot, procedural placeholder

copy.title: From one harbour to a whole ocean
copy.deck: sample readings a day, sharded. A query fans out, each shard answers with its own top ten, a merge keeps the best.
copy.fine: A simple timing model on sample data. Not a measurement.

copy.title: Three lines
copy.deck: Send a place, get the nearest stations back. Fictional API, sample key.

tabs.label: Python
tabs.code:
from tidewell import Client
db = Client(api_key="tw_sample_key")
hits = db.near("harbour mouth at dusk", top_k=3)

tabs.label: TypeScript
curl
tabs.code:
curl https://api.tidewell.example/v1/near \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer tw_sample_key" \
  -d '{"q":"harbour mouth at dusk","top_k":3}'

copy.title: Priced by what
copy.deck: Move the sliders. Every tier is priced live, and the cheapest one that fits lights up in the lattice.
copy.fine: Invented prices for the concept. The arithmetic is shown.

faq.a: No. It is a fictional product and this is a concept page. Every number is sample data, labelled where it appears.
A brute-force nearest-item search over the sample items, run in your browser each frame. The millisecond figure is that scan on your device, not a benchmark of any service.
It sets how many nodes a graph search may visit. A larger width finds better neighbours and costs more time. The curve is a sample model.

faq.q: Where do the prices come from?
faq.a: They are invented for the concept and shown with the arithmetic, so you can check the sum.
There is none stored. The lattice is drawn in code; any art slot is a procedural placeholder until an image is generated for it.

cta.title: Ask the lattice something.
cta.body: Fictional product, so there is no key to take. The lattice is yours to move.
cta.label: Back to the lattice
